decision.context: Required legacy evidence uses lxml/libxml2 and xmlschema as two live general-purpose validators. Node primary qualification succeeded within explicit limits; the two investigated independent Node candidates failed construction/precision controls.
decision.proposal: Remove Python after implementing every mapped port. Use current libxml2-wasm observations, independently authored strict TypeScript checks of selected contracts, and pinned historical xmlschema observations with explicit remaining unqualified capabilities.
decision.acceptance: The maintainer accepted NT-CONT-01 and authorized full delivery. Gate S passes through this explicit change to the 23 methods, one secondary baseline instance and 13 SOAP calls; implementation and execution qualification remain separate requirements.
decision.consequence: The final required lane has one live general-purpose XSD engine. Contract checks provide fresh scoped evidence but do not claim a second full XSD validator or full post-schema augmentation.
decision.dependencyBoundary: Existing Node/npm/tsc/tsx/Vitest/XML tooling plus exact test-only prebuilt libxml2-wasm@0.7.2. No Python/pip/venv, JDK, native compiler, remote oracle or new general-purpose validation framework.
decision.alternative: Retaining the requirement for two full live XSD engines leaves Gate S blocked. Building a general XSD engine or maintaining/rebuilding a native wrapper requires a separate scope decision.
decision.reopenTrigger: A reproducible required API fails because the scoped contracts cannot cover a needed schema or typed-value capability, and a concrete Python implementation provides that capability after comparison with feasible Node options.

invariants: All 53 mapped methods, their loop/subcase families and module-level literal tables remain traceable; no count-only replacement.
Required baseline selection remains 6 schemas/15 instances; full selection remains 14/40. Both selections execute every migrated reference method and reject empty discovery.
A selected contract answer is never labeled general schema-construction acceptance or a second external-engine result.
Original huge-bound inputs remain byte-identical and explicitly unqualified as full schemas where unsupported; adjusted copies cannot qualify them.
Exact integer/decimal/calendar domains, original identity, lexical namespace/source witnesses and pre-allocation work limits remain intact.
Expected answers come from independent literals/reviewed source contracts, never production compiler or semantic helpers.
Historical answers keep their original engine/version/input/source identity; no relabeling as fresh Node evidence.
Missing setup, malformed/forbidden input, schema rejection, instance rejection, unsupported capability and exhausted resources remain distinguishable.
No product semantics, public formats, support-profile claims, #232/#234 proof status, draft #231 or release status changes.

reviewFindings.finding: Coverage verification and qualification recording use git show at the baseline; shallow checkouts or deleted sources may lack those objects. The existing map pins source blocks but does not contain full source bytes/module-level tables.

reviewFindings.finding: The primary huge-bound guard only matches digits and any attribute local name; legal leading-plus/whitespace bounds can bypass it and foreign annotation attributes can trigger it.
reviewFindings.action: Guard unqualified occurrence attributes on XSD particles only, using exact nonNegativeInteger lexical forms before engine allocation. Test leading plus, whitespace, zeros, exact threshold/above threshold and foreign annotations without modifying original inputs.

reviewFindings.finding: The frozen guard hashes the whole existing SOAP helper, conflicting with a pre-cutover edit of that helper.

reviewFindings.finding: The staging guard still reads the legacy allowance and npm CI scripts do not all invoke it.
reviewFindings.action: Remove allowance loading/code/file together; require the final guard in normal required CI lanes and retain draft #231 rejection controls.

reviewFindings.finding: Launcher tests still expect missing Python, and S06 discovery still names Python tests.
reviewFindings.action: Use Node setup/version, empty-discovery, changed-observation and command failure controls. Reconcile actual executed TS files, all 147 S06 entries and hashes, engine metadata, docs and registry.

reviewFindings.finding: Existing hosted jobs run only Linux and install Python; PATH aliases do not deny absolute interpreters.
reviewFindings.action: Provide verified absence or execution denial on all four OS/Node combinations before normal npm ci and execution; validate name and absolute-path negative controls, record mechanism and attempts, and block if the environment cannot enforce it.

reviewFindings.finding: Platform-sensitive local URI/path/symlink checks and worker execution are not qualified on Windows or Node 26.
reviewFindings.action: Exercise Windows drive/UNC/backslash/file-URL/namespace/resource cases and available symlink controls in the maintained Windows environment without skipping required boundary behavior.

reviewFindings.finding: Research recorders hash current sources while reading prior raw output; environment equality alone does not prove code/run correspondence.
reviewFindings.action: Capture source/input/engine hashes at execution and refuse stale raw-result/source mismatches before generating any new qualification record. Preserve existing historical records unchanged.
